articles.title: Reds' Chase Burns is nearing an important milestone in his development
articles.description: Cincinnati Reds 23-year-old pitcher Chase Burns is looking to reach 30 starts in 2026. He made start No. 29 in the Reds victory over the Cubs Friday.

articles.title: Reds claim versatile Oswaldo Cabrera from Yankees with eye on 2027
articles.description: The Cincinnati Reds hope Oswaldo Cabrera's on-field performance can match his 'off the charts' makeup after claiming him off waivers from the Yankees.

articles.title: Reds RHP Julian Garcia (elbow) to IL, RHP Julian Aguiar recalled
articles.description: Cincinnati Reds right-hander Julian Aguiar, who debuted in 2024 before Tommy John surgery wiped out his 2025, was called up to pair with Chase Burns.

articles.title: Why Cubs' Ian Happ is the Cincinnati Reds' prototype free agent target
articles.description: Chicago Cubs LF Ian Happ, the former UC star, is a pending free agent with 4 Gold Gloves and a career .784 OPS. It's 1.002 in 66 career games at GABP.

articles.title: Another day, another team clinches against Reds as Dodgers win NL West
articles.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers outscored the Cincinnati Reds 41-15 to win 6 of 7 meetings over an 11-day span. That included an 8-2 win Thursday at GABP.

articles.title: Reds roster move coming? Tyler Stephenson exits but avoids injury?

articles.title: Despite criticism, Reds front office expected to return intact
articles.description: The Reds, who avoided a winless six-game road trip with a win over the Brewers Sunday, plan to maintain continuity with their front office management team.

articles.title: Is Cincinnati Reds manager Terry Francona a lame duck?
articles.description: "I love working with the guy, and I couldn't see myself working with somebody else in that role," Reds president Nick Krall said of Terry Francona.

articles.title: Cincinnati Reds make wrong kind of history in another high-scoring loss
articles.description: MLB's top two teams have clobbered the Cincinnati Reds so hard the past three games it made ignominious history for baseball's oldest franchise.
